headline: High risk of shared-repo prompt injection and data leakage; dexter’s autonomous API use plus Aider’s git writes create cascading error and compliance exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and writes git-tracked files in a shared repo, and dexter writes to .dexter/scratchpad/ while using autonomous execution. That creates a plausible content bridge where dexter-generated text can be consumed by Aider as trusted file input. No direct parser evidence is shown, so I do not escalate to high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace path, file content can cross from dexter to Aider.
IF Aider is instructed to treat repo files as authoritative, injected instructions in shared files can influence its actions.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different repos or worktrees.
Disable automatic ingestion of scratchpad or generated files into Aider prompts.
Add a review step before Aider acts on any dexter-written file.
Use file allowlists for Aider input paths.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared files and reject untrusted instruction-like content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider has broad network egress and handles model-provider API keys, while dexter sends data to multiple third-party APIs including OpenAI, Financial Datasets, Exa, Tavily, and LangSmith. If they share a workspace, source code or financial data can flow into both agents’ outbound requests, creating a realistic exfiltration path with sensitive data exposure.
conditions: IF the two agents share files or environment variables, sensitive code or financial data can be transmitted by either agent.
IF dexter processes financial data in the same workspace Aider edits, that data may be exposed to external APIs.
mitigations: Run the agents under separate OS users.
Remove shared access to secrets and API keys.
Keep financial data and source code in separate directories.
Block outbound network except to approved endpoints.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention and egress proxy policies.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider can execute shell commands, modify git state, read/write the filesystem, and spawn subprocesses; dexter has broad network egress and autonomous execution. In a shared repo, both can mutate the same working tree and external state without documented locking, so concurrent writes and git-state conflicts are a default danger.
conditions: IF both agents target the same git repository, concurrent commits or rewrites can conflict.
IF dexter and Aider run simultaneously, one agent can overwrite the other's filesystem changes.
mitigations: Serialize access to the shared repository.
Use separate branches per agent.
Require manual merge review before commit.
Pause one agent while the other writes.
requires-engineering: add distributed locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider’s git-commit workflow can turn dexter’s outputs into committed changes, and dexter’s autonomous execution can generate unverified recommendations or data. Because Aider can act on repo content and dexter can produce API-backed outputs, a mistaken dexter result can cascade into committed code or downstream actions without a strong verification barrier.
conditions: IF Aider treats dexter-produced files or summaries as authoritative, errors can be committed to git.
IF dexter’s API-derived outputs are used as facts without review, downstream actions can be wrong at scale.
mitigations: Require human review before commits.
Add a verification checklist for dexter outputs.
Compare dexter outputs against a second source before acting.
Limit Aider to draft-only mode for dexter-generated content.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking and provenance tracking.

E_compliance.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history, while dexter touches financial and market data and sends it to third-party APIs. That creates a compliance mismatch risk around retention, logging, and data residency if the same regulated dataset or secrets are present in the shared workflow. The profiles do not prove a specific residency breach, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is processed in the same workflow as source code, retention and logging policies may diverge.
IF either agent stores outputs in shared logs, subject-rights or deletion handling can become inconsistent.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces.
Review retention settings for all API providers.
Disable verbose logging for sensitive runs.
Document which agent handles which data class.
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across both toolchains.
